posts.subject: Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 auto-dimming / brightness drops when switching from bright to dark webpages
posts.author: Hieu2736
posts.message_html:
I'm having a really annoying issue with my Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 monitor. Whenever I switch from a bright website (like a white Google page) to a low-brightness/dark website (like Reddit in dark mode), the monitor automatically dims itself or changes its contrast .

I have already turned off DCR and other settings but it still dims ( please help )

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 auto-dimming / brightness drops when switching from bright to dark webpages
posts.author: Hassen_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello Hieu2736,

Welcome to Lenovo Community, and thank you for describing the issue with your Legion 27QD‑10 monitor. I understand how distracting it is when the brightness or contrast shifts between bright and dark pages.

Since you’ve already turned off DCR, please also check these items to help stop the automatic dimming behavior:

  1. Monitor OSD settings – Review options such as HDR, local dimming, dynamic brightness, smart image/scenario modes, eye care/low blue light, or auto brightness. Disable them and test again.

  2. Windows display settings – Go to Settings > System > Display. If HDR is available, turn it off for testing. Disable any adaptive brightness options. In Intel, AMD, or NVIDIA graphics settings, look for content‑adaptive brightness or dynamic contrast and turn them off.

  3. Connection test – Try another cable, switch between DisplayPort and HDMI, or test the monitor with another device to see if the behavior remains.

  4. Factory reset – Use the monitor menu to perform a reset. Afterward, only change the minimum needed settings and test before adjusting further.

If the dimming still happens after these steps, please let us know the results so we can continue with more targeted guidance.

Best regards, Hassen_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Legion 27QD-10 auto-dimming / brightness drops when switching from bright to dark webpages
posts.author: Hieu2736
posts.message_html:
1. HDR has been disabled. The monitor's OSD does not contain options for local dimming, dynamic brightness, scenario modes, low blue light, or auto brightness.
1. HDR is unavailable, and Windows 10 lacks adaptive brightness options for this setup. Additionally, Nvidia settings do not list content-adaptive brightness or dynamic contrast.
3. Using an HDMI connection caps the refresh rate at 144Hz, so I use USB-C instead. Consequently, the display routes through the integrated CPU graphics rather than the discrete GPU.
4. I have already attempted this without success; the screen dimming persists.

the screen still dimming
